subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should sandbox browser support be added as narrow external CDP/noVNC config, or should it wait for a broader browser backend/plugin interface?
rationale: The request adds new configuration and changes browser-control security boundaries, while current project guidance favors core seams or plugin APIs over one-off core behavior when optional capability can be generalized.

options.title: Design browser backend contract first
options.body: Use the broader browser backend/plugin interface as the canonical product direction, with external CDP/noVNC as one possible implementation.

options.title: Add explicit external endpoint mode
options.body: Accept a narrow core config surface for externally managed CDP/noVNC endpoints with security review, docs, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Defer core change
options.body: Keep Docker-managed sandbox browser as the only supported sandbox browser path until demand or a plugin API gap is confirmed by maintainers.

recommendation.title: Design browser backend contract first
recommendation.body: Use the broader browser backend/plugin interface as the canonical product direction, with external CDP/noVNC as one possible implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the strongest recent ownership signal across sandbox browser, config hardening, and docs surfaces central to this product decision.
